children: Food inflation in India, which was roughly 6% in August, is unlikely to persist towards the end of the year, Chief Economic Adviser V Anantha Nageswaran said on Tuesday, as a shortfall in monsoon is "manageable" and crop output is expected to be good.
Food and beverages account for 36.75% of India's consumer price index basket, which is used to measure retail inflation.
Here are more details from his address:
India's monsoon rainfall deficit currently stands at about 15%, while summer crop sowing is only 2%-3% lower than last year, he said at an event organised by industry body ASSOCHAM.
Output for most summer sown crops is expected to be strong despite rainfall volatility.
Global risks have resurfaced but Indian economy is likely to remain resilient.
Uncertainties have resurfaced due to the developments in the Middle East in the last five days, and it remains to be seen whether the economy can ride through them as it did between March and July.
The government is closely monitoring these developments and will assess its response as the situation evolves.
India's policy stance will remain supportive, with a focus on maintaining macroeconomic stability while pursuing deregulation and improving the ease of doing business.
